comment: The statement that federated implementations are particularly useful where continuous central connectivity cannot be assumed is only partially correct. Federated nodes may still depend on remote data sources, identity services, or online discovery. Federation does not automatically provide offline resilience.

public.text: The statement that federated implementations are particularly useful where continuous central connectivity cannot be assumed is only partially correct. Federated nodes may still depend on remote data sources, identity services, or online discovery. Federation does not automatically provide offline resilience.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify that resilience in low-connectivity settings requires local availability, caching, asynchronous exchange, conflict resolution, and store-and-forward capabilities, regardless of whether the wider topology is federated.
